leads.summary: Related Battle.net PRs' launcher fixtures break when this PR's scale call is retained
leads.location: bin/omarchy-launch-battlenet:49; related PRs #8932 test/shell.d/battlenet-test.sh, #13195 test/shell.d/battlenet-test.sh, #13354 test/shell.d/launch-battlenet-test.sh
leads.consequence: #8932's changes to the launcher merge textually with this head, but its launcher test sets PATH=$mock_bin:$PATH, not $ROOT/bin. The merged launcher exits 127 at the new helper invocation rather than reaching its mocked umu-run; the test fails. #13195 and #13354 edit the same launcher hunk and git merge-file produces conflict markers. Resolving those conflicts by retaining the scale call also causes their new launcher tests to exit 127 for the same PATH omission. Resolving by discarding the call instead silently removes scaling. Update each fixture's PATH to include $ROOT/bin (with stubbed helper dependencies) or stub this helper explicitly, and retain the call on the launch branch when resolving conflicts. This is a combined-PR integration/test issue, not a failure of this PR's own test.
leads.triage: verified_factual_not_published; Related open PRs #8932/#13195/#13354 launcher fixtures lack the new helper on PATH (confirmed #8932 test PATH="$mock_bin:$PATH"); integration concern for whichever PR merges second, not a defect in #12432.

leads.summary: The scale fixture cannot detect loss of the agent-session waiting and Proton verb safeguards
leads.consequence: Two plausible regressions in the new helper pass every test: replacing wait_for_rest with immediate success writes the DPI while Wine children can still be alive, and dropping PROTON_VERB=run from umu() defaults umu to waitforexitandrun. For an agent-held session, GE-Proton then calls wineserver -w before starting wineboot, so the helper/desktop launch can wait indefinitely rather than stop the agent. The mock kills all its stand-ins synchronously on the exact wineboot command and never checks PROTON_VERB. Add a delayed-kill stand-in and assert reg add does not run until its process is gone; assert the umu-run mock receives PROTON_VERB=run on wineboot and reg add.
leads.triage: sent_to_opus_confirmed; (a) published as Optional test improvement, (b) private; Opus followup-1 Q1: both mutants survive; (b) guards a hypothetical refactor.

leads.summary: Concurrent first launches can kill each other's in-flight DPI registry command
leads.consequence: Two simultaneous invocations can both decide the prefix is idle before either begins reg add. If the first's Wine reg.exe then appears, the second classifies its C:\windows\system32 command line as a system process and runs wineboot -k -s, terminating the first registry writer. The first helper nonetheless exits 0 and its caller launches; the second writer may recover the DPI, but if it fails or arrives after the first client starts, the client uses the old DPI. The interleaving and termination are verified with isolated tagged processes, not live Wine; whether this is frequent enough to require a per-prefix lock should be tested using two simultaneous fresh Battle.net launches with the pinned Wine runtime, or source-traced with precise startup timing.
leads.triage: sent_to_opus_confirmed_private; Opus followup-1 Q2: pre-existing since b7f1ea0, stub model only, worst case one launch at old DPI; not published.

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** at `7cd1636`, both findings from the [earlier review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12432#issuecomment-5830395973) are resolved, as described in the [author's reply](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12432#issuecomment-5845296532). The two new commits introduce no regressions in the checked scope.

| Earlier finding | Status | Change |
|---|---|---|
| Session detection misses a symlinked prefix path | Resolved in `fba34ee` | `COMPAT=$(realpath -m -- "$PREFIX")`, matched as `STEAM_COMPAT_DATA_PATH=$COMPAT` |
| `wineboot -k` restarts the prefix's autostart programs | Resolved in `7cd1636` | `umu wineboot -k -s` |

**Verified:**

- **Resolved prefix.** umu 1.4.4 exports `Path(WINEPREFIX).expanduser().resolve(strict=False)` as `STEAM_COMPAT_DATA_PATH` (`umu_run.py` L154, L290). 1.2.9 and 1.3.0 also resolve the prefix. In an isolated comparison of 13 layouts, `realpath -m` gives the same path as umu in all but a symlink loop, where no prefix can exist. The matching layouts include a symlinked `~/Games` (absolute, relative, chained or under a symlinked directory), a symlinked prefix, a symlinked `$HOME`, `$HOME` with a trailing slash, and missing or dangling paths. With stand-in processes carrying umu's value, the new helper leaves a game session alone and stops an agent-only session in each of the eight layouts that can hold a session. The earlier helper handled only the plain layout.
- **`-k -s`.** At the Wine commit GE-Proton11-7 pins (`46b29104`), `wineboot.c` returns right after `kill_processes( shutdown )` when `-s` is set (L1942-1944), so no services, Run entries or Startup items are started. The two GE patches touching `programs/wineboot` do not change that path. Plain `-k` already killed every process except the desktop, so `-s` only adds the desktop process, and only in sessions the in-use check has cleared.
- **Tests.** `test/shell.d/battlenet-scale-test.sh` passes on the head (13 of 13 runs, 3 of them under full CPU load) and on the head merged with `quattro` at `387fcf5` (5 of 5, clean merge). Each fix's case fails without its fix: reverting only the resolved-path match writes `/d 192` into the live symlinked game session, and dropping `-s` fails the agent-only case. The full CLI and shell suites show the same failing files with and without the PR, on both the PR's parent and `quattro` at `387fcf5`.

**Optional test improvement:** the `umu-run` mock ends the stand-in processes inside the `wineboot -k -s` call, so a helper whose `wait_for_rest` returns immediately still passes all 11 assertions. Ending the stand-ins shortly after that call returns, and checking at `reg add` that none of them still has an environment in `/proc` (killed stand-ins can linger as zombies), makes the test catch that mutation; the current head passes the stricter version. This test design predates the new commits.

**PR description:** "The change" still says the idle session is stopped with `wineboot -k`. The helper now uses `wineboot -k -s`. The hardware results in the description were measured before both commits.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** follow-up on the two new commits, `fba34ee` and `7cd1636`. Source review of the helper and test against umu-launcher (1.2.9, 1.3.0, 1.4.4) and GE-Proton11-7 with its pinned Wine tree. The PR test, the path-resolution comparison, the diagnostic mutations and the full suites ran in an isolated sandbox with stubbed `hyprctl` and `umu-run` and stand-in processes. No Wine, Proton, umu, Battle.net or Hyprland was executed, so real session shutdown timing with `-k -s` and on-screen scaling were not verified.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
